evidence.summary: capture_angles 4 views vs Welsh cottage references: walls/door/windows/foundation match the brief, but both gable-end views (90/270 deg) show the two RoofSlab parts INVERTED into a V-valley (butterfly) instead of an A-frame pitched gable - gable wedges protrude above the slabs, the RidgeCap sits in the valley, the chimney rises from the valley center, and the front view shows an open gap between wall head and floating eave.

reasons: Roof slabs pitched the wrong way: V-valley instead of A-frame gable ridge - the defining cottage silhouette is broken
No true ridge; RidgeCap is at the valley bottom, chimney emerges from the valley not the ridge
Visible gap between wall top and roof plane on the front elevation (sky/interior showing)
Fails the building rubric's coherent-massing/roof-reads-as-roof bar despite correct door/window/foundation detailing

config.style: whitewashed Welsh-style cottage: slate-white walls, dark pitched gable roof with ridge cap and eave overhang, red door + red-trimmed cross-mullion windows, cobblestone foundation, stone chimney

added side gable wedges (rise 6), two angled roof slabs with overhang + ridge cap, cobblestone chimney
dressed openings: glass panes with white cross mullions, red trim/sills, red plank door + stone doorstep
verified structurally (bounds, ground contact, doorway raycast) since capture sidecar was down
